messages:
deploybot: Scheduled unpin: runtime v3.5.2 -> v3.6.0 on canary pool at 2026-03-22T10:00Z. Affected model tags: quant-v5a, llama4q-quant. Opt-out: react :no_entry: within 30m or run `deploybot opt-out --id 2765432101`.

devin: tagging because we have a few dedicated tenants pinned to sdk@1.4.x that map to runtime-3.5.2 — any compatibility checks?

maria: ran a quick inventory: 6 dedicated tenants pinned, 2 longseq heavy, 1 streaming-heavy. All flagged in the release ticket.

jen: last time we saw quant-v5a on longseq we hit progressive memory pressure after ~30k tokens. Not immediate OOM but tail failures.

anjali: routing policy can fallback to non-quant variants, but that tag isn't enabled for these canary pools yet. I can enable for canary only if we want.

pm-oliver: proposal: enable fallback for canary, run focused preflight on longseq + streaming, and add a temporary per-tenant longseq throttle for canary (10 TPS max) during observation. If preflight looks good, proceed. If not, abort and pin back.

sara: starting preflight now with 50 longseq + streaming mixes. Will collect heap traces. ETA 35m.

devin: for rollback automation I drafted an emergency pinback helper:```
# emergency pinback
deploybot cancel-unpin --id 2765432101
deploybot pin-runtime --version 3.5.2 --models "quant-v5a,llama4q-quant"
```
Can deploybot run both atomically?

deploybot: Cancel accepted only if requested >20m prior to scheduled start. After that, cancel is manual and pin-runtime will require operator approval. No atomic two-step supported yet.

maria: timeline looks tight. recommend pushing unpin start by 3h to finish preflight + stakeholder notif.

jen: +1. also please enable throttling gate for canary now, limits: 10 TPS per-tenant for requests >20k tokens.

anjali: enabling fallback routing tag: "fallback=non-quant-longseq" for canary pools. Pushing in 8m. Will not affect prod pools.

support-bot: Notifying support channels about possible degradations for pinned customers. Message queued to #support-notify.

sara: preflight results: ran 50 requests, 2 degraded tails (latency spikes x2), 1 soft OOM recovered by GC during generation on a 48k prompt. Attached logs: https://artifacts.internal/reports/2765432101-preflight.log

devin: soft OOM recovered with GC is acceptable if fallback routing prevents hard OOMs. If fallback didn't trigger for the failing requests then we need to hold.

anjali: checked traces. For the request that hit soft OOM, routing did fall back for subsequent retries but not the first attempt due to routing decision latency. I can shorten the routing re-eval window to 150ms, but that requires a tiny edge rollout.

pm-oliver: decision: delay unpin by 3h (new start 2026-03-22T13:00Z), enable fallback for canary, add throttling gate, shorten routing re-eval window for canary only, prepare manual operator pinback steps. If further regressions appear, abort and re-pin runtime v3.5.2.

maria: updating release ticket with pinback runbook, operator checklist, and list of pinned tenants: https://tickets.internal/REL-2765432101

jen: sending a heads-up to the dedicated-account owners for the 6 tenants now. Will post in #dedicated-notify.

sara: uploading full heap traces and latency histograms to artifact link above. Summary: mean latency +12% on canary quant variant, 1 recoverable OOM, no catastrophic failures.

devin: thanks all. delaying unpin. if anyone sees new red flags, reply here. Otherwise we'll reconvene 1h before the new start time for a final go/no-go.

deploybot: Unpin start delayed to 2026-03-22T13:00Z by request from devin. To cancel: react with :no_entry: or run `deploybot cancel-unpin --id 2765432101` if within policy window. Manual pinback steps added to ticket.
